{{recipesummary|category=Beverage recipes|servings=12|time=Prep: 20 minutes
Ferment: 1–2 days|difficulty=2 }} {{recipe}} | [[:Category:Fermented food recipes|Fermented food recipes]] '''Ginger beer''' is a traditional fermented drink that can be made as either a soft drink or an alcoholic drink. Make it in a carboy with more sugar or [[Cookbook:Malt Extract|malt extract]] and with longer fermentation time to get alcoholic ginger beer. ==Ingredients== * 100–300 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]] fresh [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] root, peeled and [[Cookbook:Grater|grated]] * 1 whole [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]], [[Cookbook:Zest|zested]] and [[Cookbook:Juice|juiced]] OR 2 [[Cookbook:Tsp|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Cream of Tartar|cream of tartar]] mixed with lemon extract or zest to make a lemon juice substitute. * 500 grams [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * [[Cookbook:Water|Water]] * Fermentation starter (see note) ==Procedure== # Simmer the ginger, lemon zest and sugar in about 1.5 L water for about 10 minutes. # If using yeast as the fermentation starter, rehydrate the yeast in a glass of warm water for 5 minutes. # Add the lemon juice and enough water to get 10 L to the fermenter (see note). # Let the mixture sit in the fermenter until it has started bubbling well, which should take 8–12 hours with yeast or longer with kefir grains. # Bottle into PET bottles or other food-safe bottles. # When the bottles are hard (not just firm) from the carbonation, put them into the fridge for storage. # Serve cold. ==Notes, tips, and variations== * For the fermentation starter, you can use [[Cookbook:Kefir|kefir grains]] or tibicos, ginger beer plant, ginger bug, ale yeast, or [[Cookbook:Yeast|bread yeast]]. * Lemon juice is to provide acidity as well as flavor. * For a fermenter, you can use anything from an old PET water bottle to a food-grade bucket or a large stainless-steel pot; don't use copper or aluminium. * The water used should be free of chlorine if possible (e.g. boiled and cooled, or filtered, or bottled spring water). This is because chlorine (or chloramine) will inhibit the fermentation a little. Use what you've got, but best results will be obtained without the chlorine. * Once the ginger beer is fermenting, as evidenced by lots of tiny bubbles rising to the surface, it can be used as a [[Cookbook:Leavening Agent|leavening agent]]. Simply replace the water and yeast in a [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] recipe with ginger beer, and leave to rise as normal. * If left to ferment longer (about a week) a yeasty colony called a ginger beer plant will develop. Carbonation will also increase, greatly raising the chances for bottle (or other container) exploding; therefore, it is advisable to use a carboy or suitable container with an airlock. [[Category:Fermented recipes]] [[Category:Recipes for alcoholic beverages]] [[Category:Recipes with metric units]] [[Category:Recipes using cream of tartar]] [[Category:Recipes using fresh ginger]]
